input_oneliner: 72F, 50 pack-year smoker, day 2 admit for pyelonephritis, wheezing and short of breath since midnight, sat 90% on 2L

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about known COPD diagnosis or prior spirometry, home inhalers, and prior exacerbations needing steroids or intubation
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Self-reported COPD and heavy pack-year history are the best-validated bedside predictors of airflow obstruction

reference_targets_freetext.item: Forced expiratory time (timed forced exhalation, >=9 s)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Prolonged forced expiratory time is the best-performing bedside sign of airflow obstruction

reference_targets_freetext.item: Wheeze and prolonged expiratory phase on auscultation
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Wheeze modestly raises likelihood of obstruction; already reported by nursing, so confirmatory

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about change in sputum volume and purulence and increase in dyspnea over baseline (Anthonisen criteria)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Defines an exacerbation and its severity

reference_targets_freetext.item: Observe work of breathing: accessory muscle use, pursed-lip breathing, ability to speak full sentences, respiratory rate
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Work of breathing grades severity and predicts need for escalation

reference_targets_freetext.item: JVP (jugular venous pressure) to look for concurrent heart failure
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Cardiac asthma mimics an obstructive exacerbation

reference_targets_freetext.item: Compare breath sounds side to side; percuss for unilateral hyperresonance (pneumothorax)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Pneumothorax in emphysema presents as sudden dyspnea and must not be nebulized away

off_bedside_acceptable: venous or arterial blood gas for hypercapnia
should_not_recommend: Titrate oxygen to saturation above 94% without assessing for hypercapnia (somnolence, asterixis)
Treat as COPD flare without examining for unilateral absent breath sounds
Rely on wheeze alone to exclude heart failure without volume examination

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: presenting symptom: wheeze -> sudden right-sided chest pain
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: 72F, 50 pack-year smoker, day 2 admit for pyelonephritis, sudden right-sided chest pain and short of breath since midnight, sat 90% on 2L
perturbation_pair.expected_change: Compare breath sounds side to side; percuss for unilateral hyperresonance becomes must_have and pneumothorax rises to top of differential; COPD history remains must_have; Forced expiratory time drops to should-still-include; Wheeze remains should-still-include; Anthonisen sputum question drops; Calf circumference asymmetry >3 cm (pulmonary embolism) is a new item.
